selection_reasoning: Mining an oak log is a fundamental, observable, and verifiable task in Minecraft. It requires the player to locate an oak tree in the scene and break the oak_log block. This task is straightforward, does not require deep Minecraft domain knowledge (just approach a tree and mine it), and is easily verifiable by checking if the player has obtained an oak_log in their inventory. As a single atomic task, no dependency edges are needed.

milestones.description: Uses inventory_has because mining an oak_log block in survival mode causes the oak_log item to drop and be picked up into the player's inventory. The player starts with an empty inventory and there are no oak_log items in the scene other than as placed blocks, so any oak_log in inventory must have been mined.

scene_description: A flat grass clearing with two hand-built oak trees placed within easy reach of the player spawn. The player starts in survival mode with an empty inventory during clear daytime weather. Tree 1 is at relative (5,0,5) with 5 oak_log blocks and a leaf canopy. Tree 2 is at relative (-4,0,-3) with 5 oak_log blocks and leaves. Both trees have trunks starting at ground level, making them immediately accessible for bare-hand mining. A 21x11x21 area is cleared around spawn to ensure flat, unobstructed terrain.
task_text: Mine an oak log from one of the nearby oak trees.
design_notes: Two oak trees on opposite sides of spawn on a flat grass clearing. Tree 1 at (5,0,5): 5 logs + 13 leaf blocks forming a canopy. Tree 2 at (-4,0,-3): 5 logs + 5 leaf blocks (smaller canopy). Both within 7 blocks of spawn, easily reachable. Player is in survival mode and can mine oak_log by hand (~4 seconds). The flat grass platform ensures no terrain obstacles. The /fill air command clears the immediate area for clean navigation. Natural terrain beyond the 21-block radius may provide additional trees but the placed trees are sufficient.
